mlb_moneyline_v2.correction_note: SUPERSEDES this entry's original 2026-08-09 version, which froze 'primary_moneyline_model: xgb_two_head' together with 'score_distribution_family: negative_binomial' as if that were one validated combination. It was not: XGBoostTwoHeadModel(seed=42)'s constructor default is method='independent_poisson', and every real call site that selected xgb_two_head (train_mlb_score_model_comparison.py, train_mlb_calibration_comparison.py, train_mlb_calibrated_ensemble_comparison.py) only ever constructed it that way -- negative_binomial was validated separately, only against MLBTwoHeadModel (sklearn heads), in train_mlb_distribution_comparison.py. The two winners were combined post hoc without ever being fit and OOF-scored together. Fixed by running the real Cartesian comparison (2 head families x 3 distributions, each cross-fit calibrated with all 4 real methods) in train_mlb_head_distribution_cartesian.py -- outputs/rebuild/mlb_head_distribution_cartesian.json. The real winner picked as one exact validated combination: head_family=xgboost, distribution=negative_binomial, calibration=temperature (cross_fit_log_loss=0.6927, cross_fit_brier=0.2498, cross_fit_ece=0.0326, n=168) -- xgboost+negative_binomial does turn out to be the real winner, but it is now actually validated together, not assembled from separate experiments. Also re-ran the Task 15 ensemble comparison using each head family's own real best-validated distribution (train_mlb_corrected_ensemble_comparison.py -- outputs/rebuild/mlb_corrected_ensemble_comparison.json): conclusion unchanged (ensemble adds no value; single calibrated xgb_two_head wins). test_start was also moved forward from 2026-08-07T01:45Z to 2026-08-08T02:20Z, strictly after the real games (through 2026-08-08T02:15Z, dataset_hash e0c513aa4a544211980f7095da0de69ad3cb647a75981cbdb3c46512834ee2eb) this correction's own comparisons used for selection -- the original boundary was stale once this correction re-ran model selection on a freshly refreshed scoreboard that extended past it.
mlb_moneyline_v2.note: Task 18 (prepared, not evaluated): replacement prospective final test for mlb_moneyline, chronologically strictly after every real game used for model-family/calibration/ensemble selection. test_end is intentionally open (null) -- zero real completed games exist past the cutoff yet, so there is nothing to evaluate; the range will be closed and evaluated once enough new games accumulate, and never before. This test must remain untouched (no peeking) until that evaluation is deliberately performed.

minimum_sample_before_evaluation.rationale: Predeclared before any real v2 game has been evaluated, per MLB-8 (multi-sport execution spec) -- never inspect aggregate v2 metrics before this many real completed games exist in the test window. 100 is not derived from a formal power calculation; it is chosen to sit meaningfully above the already-consumed mlb_moneyline final test's n=21 (explicitly flagged small-sample, accuracy/brier not trustworthy at that size) and to match this session's own real precedent for when a calibration method is trusted with more flexibility (isotonic's real n<100 -> no-op fallback in calibration.py). Disclosed as a reasonable floor, not a rigorously derived minimum-detectable-effect sample size.
minimum_sample_before_evaluation.enforcement: scripts/check_mlb_v2_readiness.py reports only committed mlb_moneyline_v2_frozen_v1 prediction count in [test_start, now), with a real observed timestamp at or before the decision cutoff. Completed scoreboard games without a committed v2 prediction never count. The script explicitly refuses to compute or print aggregate accuracy/log-loss/Brier.
